uncited: This family provides geometric primitives and cross-sectional views to inspect the spatial extent, selection state, and internal structure of voxel data during rendering.

It solves the problem of spatial orientation and debugging by overlaying wireframes or slices onto the framebuffer, distinct from [Binary Volume Rendering (Opacity Thresholding)](1015-binary-volume-rendering-opacity-thresholding.md) which visualizes the volume content itself rather than its container or structure.

All methods in this family operate on the principle of rendering auxiliary geometry or post-processing textures to provide visual feedback about the voxel data's location or bounds, without contributing to the final volumetric appearance.
They typically rely on standard OpenGL rasterization states (depth testing, blending) and simple geometric primitives (lines, triangles, quads).
The specific AABB geometry generation and Voxel Visualization post-processing steps are documented in the source code comments and implementation of that project.
The Bounding Box Drawing method reflects common practices in OpenGL-based voxel debuggers for selection feedback.
